This scholarship is for applicants who are nationals of India, are classified as 'Overseas' for fee purposes and have been accepted to study an eligible Masters course at Sussex starting in September 2026 or January 2027.
To be eligible for this scholarship, you must:
Be classified as ‘overseas’ for fee purposes
Be taking up a place on a full time Masters degree, starting September 2026 or January 2027
You are not eligible for this scholarship if your tuition fees are fully sponsored
You are not eligible for this scholarship if you are going to study any of the following:
Courses at Brighton and Sussex Medical School (BSMS)
MA Governance, Development and Public Policy
MA Poverty, Policy and Development Practice
MA Power, Participation and Social Change
Degrees in Social work (if receiving an NHS bursary)
Masters funded by the research councils (e.g. ESRC 1+3 funding)
The scholarship is applied automatically if you meet the eligibility criteria. If this changes at any time, the scholarship will be removed.

Confirmation of the scholarship will be sent by email after you receive an offer of a place to study at Sussex and information about the scholarship will be included in your CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) for your visa application. If the scholarship information is not showing on your CAS, please contact the Admissions Office:

Students must be self-financing to receive the scholarship. If you confirm that you are being sponsored, or that your tuition fees are being paid by sponsor, employer or other funding provider, then the scholarship offer will be revoked.
The scholarship is awarded as a tuition fee reduction for each year of full-time study at Sussex. The scholarship is not available for placement/study abroad years or if you are required to resit.

Advice for dual nationals: in order to receive the Sussex India Scholarship, you may be asked to provide evidence to the University of your Indian nationality (such as a passport or other form of official government identification which confirms citizenship). If you are planning to apply for your Student Visa with another passport, then please note that you may also be required to present evidence of your Indian nationality during the visa application process and arrival in the UK as the Sussex India Scholarship will be included on your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) document.
